answer: Parallel-Proof Work Windows: each agent identity must complete a random challenge at dawn, and the proof broadcast as a whisper is checked against a global time-bound key. A valid proof requires a unique hardware clock signature, so fabricated identities cannot share one machine without one crashing the other's timing check. Launching N sybils costs N crystal-grade clock attestations plus N concurrent power draws, making mass coordination linearly expensive at the hardware layer.
